cues: Gabriel García Márquez, known as Gabo, was born in nineteen twenty seven in Aracataca, a small town in Colombia, and raised by his grandparents.
His grandmother told stories of ghosts and omens in a flat, matter of fact voice, and that voice became his own.
A journalist turned novelist, he wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude and won the Nobel Prize in nineteen eighty two.
This story is from nineteen sixty eight.
